By continuing you agree to the XHere Terms and Community guidelines. There is no tolerance for objectionable content or abusive users: you can report or block anyone, and moderators remove what breaks the rules.
Posting means you follow the Community guidelines. Anyone can report a drop.
Thanks. A moderator will look at it. Reports are private, and the author isn\'t told who sent one.

Before you post a safety drop
Describe what happened, not who. Don\'t name or describe people, and leave out house numbers.
Safety posts are unverified community reports, not official records. XHere is not a way to contact the police.
A moderator reviews this before anyone else sees it.
The map shows an area of about %1$d m, not the exact spot.
Incident reports are only available where a local police tip line is set up. For now that\'s the Jamestown area. In an emergency call 911.
Sent for review. It appears on the map once a moderator approves it.
Posted with reduced trust. It stays on the map and does not count toward quests or campaigns.
A JSON file with your profile, drops (with their exact spots), confirmations, reports you sent, blocks, and hidden drops.
Your data is ready. Choose where to save or send it.
Couldn\'t prepare your data. Try again.
Want a copy first? Use Download my data before you delete.
XHere is for information about places, not about hunting people. These rules match the category rules the app enforces.
Describe the place and what happened. Don\'t describe a person.
Be accurate. Say what you saw, and don\'t dress up a guess as a fact.
Keep phone numbers and email addresses out of the text.
In an emergency, call 911. XHere is not a reporting channel to police.
Don\'t sell or give away weapons, drugs, or other regulated items.

Harassment, threats, or hate toward a person or group. Sexual content involving anyone under 18. Private contact details or documents. Impersonation, spam, and ads unrelated to the place. Naming or describing a suspect, a witness, or a neighbor so someone could pick them out.

Open a drop to report it, report its author, block its author, or hide just that drop for yourself. Blocking hides drops both ways: you won\'t see theirs and they won\'t see yours. Two reports hide a safety drop automatically until a moderator looks. Other categories hide after the number set on the category, usually three.

Safety alerts and incident reports last 72 hours. New accounts\' safety alerts are reviewed before anyone sees them. Incident reports need a Regular account, are reviewed unless you\'re Trusted, show an area of about 100 m instead of the exact spot, stay unconfirmed until two people nearby confirm them, and are only offered where a local police tip line is set up. The filter blocks contact details and words for gender, age, race, clothing, build, and similar descriptors. Incident reports also block house numbers with street names.

Zero tolerance for child sexual abuse and exploitation. That content is removed, the account is suspended, and apparent abuse material is reported to the NCMEC CyberTipline. Report it from the drop, or write to hello@xhere.world. If a child is in danger, call 911.

Moderators review reports, aiming for within 24 hours. They can approve, hide, or remove a drop, and suspend an account. Every action is kept in an audit log that can\'t be edited. If you think a decision was wrong, write to hello@xhere.world.
Nothing waiting. Pending drops and open reports show up here.
Only moderators can open the queue.
Done. It\'s in the audit log.
